changes.before: Implement logSummary(event). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: Keep useful error details in a log without copying private request data into it.

before: A diagnostic log can help connect a failed request with a status without copying the whole request. Explicitly select the fields needed for that investigation.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.
The object literal copies only requestId and status. This example assumes requestId is an application-generated safe identifier. It is not a universal sanitizer for arbitrary nested event objects.

Read the function call logSummary({"requestId":"r1","status":500,"token":"secret","body":"private"}) from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, logSummary runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
The incoming event gains a password field. What will this summary contain? The explicit projection excludes additional fields. Real logging also needs appropriate access and retention policies.
after: A log is a record of what an app did. It can help you find a failed request and see its result.
For this exercise, keep requestId and status. requestId identifies the request. status shows its HTTP result, such as 500 for a server error.
The new object names the two fields to keep. Do not copy the entire event and hope that it contains nothing private.
Reading event.requestId and event.status does not remove them from event. The function returns a new, smaller object.
Add a password field to an input. The result should still contain only requestId and status. This exercise assumes the app supplies a safe request ID.
